headline: Record Reliance profit, foreign buyers return, Wall Street tech slump

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Saturday, the thirty-first of October, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter this morning. First, Reliance Industries posted the biggest quarterly profit in its history, and Jio Platforms reported its first numbers as a listed company. Second, foreign investors finally turned buyers. They ended a nine-week selling streak, and the Nifty closed back above 23,000. Third, a storm on Wall Street. Worries about how much Big Tech is spending on artificial intelligence sent the Nasdaq down nearly 3 percent overnight, and that sets a nervous tone for Monday.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Friday was a good day for the headline indices, but not for most portfolios. The Sensex rose 308 points to close at 74,459. The Nifty gained about half a percent to 23,053. That makes it about 1,200 points on the Sensex over two sessions.

But look under the surface. The midcap and smallcap indices fell as much as 2 percent, and falling shares outnumbered rising ones. Suzlon, Swiggy, STL and HFCL dropped as much as 10 percent.

The leaders were IT and pharma. The Nifty IT index rose over 2 percent, and the BSE IT index is up about 14 percent in October, its second-sharpest monthly rally in more than two decades. The Nifty Pharma index hit a record high, with Sun Pharma, Laurus, Zydus and others up as much as 6 percent. Consumer durables fell nearly 2 percent.

Among stocks, Trent jumped as much as 7 percent on strong results, and IndiGo rose over 4 percent. Godrej Consumer fell 7 percent to a four-year low on margin worries.

Now to the money flows. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth about 6,305 crore rupees over the week, according to Moneycontrol, snapping a nine-week selling streak. For October as a whole, the Nifty gained 1.9 percent to a six-month high, and the Sensex ended a two-month losing streak.

Levels to watch. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol say the short-term outlook stays positive as long as the Nifty holds 22,800. A decisive move above 23,200, one analyst said, could carry it towards 23,500 to 23,600.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
In the primary market, SEBI has cleared four more companies to raise money. Atomberg Technologies, Ratnadeep Retail, Punjab Carbonic and GNI Infrastructure all received the regulator's observations this week.

Jio's debut drew heavy borrowing. Business Standard reports that retail investors took about 234 million dollars in margin funding to trade Jio on listing day. That came weeks after a wave of margin-call selling shrank the market's margin book from a record 1.59 lakh crore rupees at the end of September to 1.51 lakh crore rupees.

Two big block deals. Tencent sold its stake in Swiggy for about 982 crore rupees, and Swiggy fell nearly 5 percent to close near its record low. And Sagility's promoter sold a 12 percent stake for about 2,395 crore rupees, with six institutions buying just over 5 percent between them.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to results, and Friday was a big one.

Reliance Industries first. Its profit hit a record, though sources quote it two ways. Profit attributable to shareholders rose about 41 percent to 25,548 crore rupees. Total profit, including minority partners, rose about 34 percent to 29,550 crore rupees. Revenue was a record 3.62 lakh crore rupees, and operating profit rose about 24 percent to 62,409 crore rupees. The oil-to-chemicals business drove it, on strong refining margins. Retail was the soft spot. Reliance Retail's gross revenue rose about 6 percent to 91,716 crore rupees, but profit fell, as the festive season shifted into the December quarter.

Jio Platforms, in its first results since listing, grew profit about 14 percent to 8,389 crore rupees on revenue of 40,475 crore rupees.

In banking and finance, Bank of Baroda's profit jumped 36 percent to 6,532 crore rupees, helped by gains from selling part of its stake in the National Stock Exchange. Gross bad loans fell to 1.78 percent, and the bank raised its loan and deposit growth guidance.

In pharma, Sun Pharma's profit fell 36 percent to 1,989 crore rupees, hit by one-time litigation and acquisition costs. Revenue still grew about 12 percent to 16,199 crore rupees, led by India and emerging markets.

In consumer names, Asian Paints' profit rose 7.5 percent to about 1,068 crore rupees on 17 percent sales growth, and it plans more staggered price hikes because of raw-material costs. Trent's revenue rose 22.5 percent to 5,788 crore rupees, with operating profit up almost 30 percent. Varun Beverages grew profit about 14 percent to 831 crore rupees, but packaging costs squeezed margins, and the shares fell about 5 percent.

Elsewhere, IndiGo posted a third straight quarterly loss, of 1,880 crore rupees, as fuel costs rose 67 percent. Coal India's profit rose 57 percent to 6,547 crore rupees, but the shares fell 3 percent as Jefferies and JM Financial cut their target prices. And Lodha Developers grew first-half profit 63 percent and expects to beat its full-year guidance.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
To the economy. The Centre's fiscal deficit for April to September was 7.14 lakh crore rupees. That's 42.1 percent of the full-year target, and about 25 percent more than a year ago. Spending rose about 11 percent, driven by capital expenditure and food subsidies, while gross tax revenue grew only about 6 percent.

India's foreign exchange reserves fell for a seventh straight week, by about 1.3 billion dollars, to around 719.8 billion dollars. A drop in the value of gold holdings did most of the damage. The rupee ended Friday 3 paise firmer, at 95.25 to the dollar.

On trade, the services surplus rose to 53.39 billion dollars in the September quarter. The government has extended the duty exemption on cotton imports to the thirty-first of December, and the Cabinet approved a 10,000 crore rupee scheme to build shipping containers in India.

From the Reserve Bank, Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said growth could have topped 8 percent without the recent global shocks. The Reserve Bank is also tightening cyber checks on banks after a run of hacks. On the other side, Niti Aayog's Ashok Lahiri flagged risks to growth if monetary policy is tightened further.

Two items for the profession. The Central Board of Indirect Taxes is holding outreach on the GST reforms from the fifty-seventh Council meeting, including a higher threshold for prosecution, which take effect from the first of April 2027. And the Institute of Chartered Accountants will issue a guidance note on the new auditor's report order for multi-state cooperative societies, notified on the fourteenth of October.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, it was a rough Friday for technology. In New York, the Dow fell about 1.1 percent, the S&P 500 1.8 percent, and the Nasdaq nearly 2.9 percent, its biggest daily fall since June. Investors fear Big Tech's spending on artificial intelligence is eating its cash. Intel plunged around 30 percent and Reddit 29 percent, while Alphabet and Amazon slid after their results.

Add to that a record crypto theft. Binance halted withdrawals after hackers stole 6.3 billion dollars, with analysts suspecting North Korea. The exchange says it will cover the losses.

The US economy, meanwhile, grew a faster-than-expected 3.4 percent. The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75 to 4 percent, and Chair Kevin Warsh said fighting inflation is the priority. Mint reports that markets now expect a possible rate hike in December.

On oil, crude is still above 110 dollars a barrel, with risks around the Strait of Hormuz. Mirae Asset Sharekhan sees Brent in a broad 105 to 120 dollar range while the US-Iran standoff lasts. Rating agency Icra estimates that if crude stays near 115 dollars and pump prices don't rise, oil marketing companies could lose over 64,000 crore rupees on petrol and diesel this year.

segments.script: An update on the Jio IPO you're following. In its first results as a listed company, Jio reported profit up about 14 percent, revenue per user up to 218 rupees 80 paise, and 9.1 million new subscribers, taking its base to 542.4 million. Monday is the first trading session after those numbers.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Now, your money. Gold has fallen to a seven-month low just ahead of Dhanteras. MCX gold slipped below 1.42 lakh rupees per ten grams on Friday, and silver has lost about 45,000 rupees a kilo in October, its steepest monthly fall this year. Strong US data and the chance of a Fed rate hike are weighing on both. Mirae Asset Sharekhan says gold's support is near 3,930 dollars an ounce, and silver could slide towards 48 dollars.

A few rules change tomorrow, the first of November. SEBI is making direct mutual fund plans the default option on fund houses' digital platforms. Regular plans still hold about 63 percent of retail fund assets. And Punjab National Bank is revising its credit card charges, including cash withdrawal fees, late payment charges and utility bill fees.

For pensioners, the pension regulator has launched a digital life certificate facility for the Unified Pension Scheme, on the Protean eGov app. Central government employees and pensioners see dearness allowance and relief go up from 60 to 63 percent, effective the first of July. House rent allowance doesn't change.

A tax calendar reminder: November brings TDS payment dates, deadlines for TDS and TCS certificates, and the extended return-filing deadline for audit cases.

That's the brief. Here's what to watch. Markets are shut for the weekend, so Monday, the second of November, is the first chance to react to the Reliance and Jio numbers, and to Friday night's tech sell-off in New York. Keep an eye on whether foreign investors keep buying, whether the Nifty holds 22,800, and on gold and silver into Dhanteras. Have a good weekend.
